title: Outsourcing in operations

match.reason: No point in the bank covers outsourcing; the closest ones deal with resources, suppliers or the internal environment, which are related ideas but not the same.

draft.title: Outsourcing in operations
card: Outsourcing is paying another business to do part of the work. Examples are making a product, running a call centre or handling payroll.
A business may outsource to cut costs. The supplier may do the job more cheaply because it does the same task for many clients.
A business may also outsource to get expertise it does not have, so it can spend its time on what it does best.
The cost is control. The supplier's staff and methods are not run by the business, so quality and timing are harder to manage.
draft.remember: Outsourcing hands work to another business, which can save money or add skill but gives up some control.

a.q: Which action is an example of outsourcing in operations?
opts: A bakery pays a firm to run its customer service line
A bakery trains its own staff to answer customer calls
A bakery buys a new oven to bake bread faster
A bakery cuts its prices to attract more customers
a.why: Outsourcing means paying another business to do part of the work. Paying a firm to run customer service fits this. Training its own staff keeps the work inside the business, so it is not outsourcing.
a.clue: Who ends up doing the work?

b.q: Priya runs a small clothing label in Perth. She pays a factory to sew all her garments. What is the main risk of this choice?
opts: She has less control over quality and delivery times
She must buy sewing machines and hire sewing staff
She loses the right to design her own garments
She can no longer sell her garments to customers
b.why: The factory's staff and methods are not managed by Priya, so she has less control over quality and timing. Buying machines and hiring staff would be needed if she did the sewing herself, not when she outsources it.
b.clue: Think about who manages the people doing the sewing.

a.best: A bakery pays a firm to run its customer service line

b.best: She has less control over quality and delivery times
